imhotep.name: Imhotep
imhotep.epigram: He read the sky and then the stone.
imhotep.kernel: Vizier, physician, the first architect with a name.

ahmes.name: Ahmes
ahmes.epigram: Here is the way of every dark thing.
ahmes.kernel: The scribe of the Rhind papyrus, and its opening line.

kidinnu.name: Kidinnu
kidinnu.epigram: He knew where the moon would be in a hundred years.

enheduanna.name: Enheduanna
enheduanna.epigram: I am the priestess; I write.
enheduanna.kernel: The first author to sign her name.

homer.name: Homer
homer.epigram: Blind, and the whole war before him.

ilimilku.name: Ilimilku
ilimilku.kernel: The Ugaritic scribe of the Baal cycle.

senenmut.name: Senenmut
senenmut.epigram: Every terrace of it was his.

amenhotepSonOfHapu.name: Amenhotep son of Hapu
amenhotepSonOfHapu.epigram: They made him a god for building.

bezalel.name: Bezalel
bezalel.epigram: Filled with the spirit, in all manner of workmanship.

eaNasir.name: Ea-nāṣir
eaNasir.epigram: You said the copper was fine.
eaNasir.kernel: The complaint tablets; the wunderkammer's patron.

kushim.name: Kushim
kushim.kernel: The first named person in writing — an accountant.

assurIdi.name: Aššur-idī
assurIdi.epigram: Send the tin by the next donkeys.
assurIdi.kernel: Old Assyrian trader of the Kanesh letters.

lamassi.name: Lamassī
lamassi.epigram: I wove the cloth; you sold it short.
lamassi.kernel: The merchant's wife whose letters survive.

ahmoseSonOfEbana.name: Ahmose son of Ebana
ahmoseSonOfEbana.epigram: I took a hand. I was given gold.

piyamaradu.name: Piyamaradu
piyamaradu.epigram: The king wrote to the king about him.

sinuhe.name: Sinuhe
sinuhe.epigram: I fled, and no one pursued.
sinuhe.kernel: The exile who fought for Retjenu and came home.

deborah.name: Deborah
deborah.epigram: The stars in their courses fought.
deborah.kernel: The judge who led at Kishon.

epicurus.name: Omar Khayyam
epicurus.epigram: Bread, a jug of wine, and the day is enough.
epicurus.kernel: A mathematician and astronomer of Nishapur in Persia. He solved cubic equations with geometry and helped to reform the calendar. He is best known for short poems about wine and the passing day; scholars dispute how many of them are his.

aristotle.name: Aristotle
aristotle.epigram: He asked what a thing was for, and wrote the answer down.
aristotle.kernel: Founder of the Lyceum; logic, physics, politics, the first library of everything.

hemiunu.name: Hemiunu
hemiunu.epigram: Two million stones, and his name on none.

ptahhotep.name: Ptahhotep
ptahhotep.kernel: The Maxims, the oldest book of advice.

zhangHeng.name: Zhang Heng
zhangHeng.epigram: The dragon dropped its ball toward the earthquake.

eratosthenes.name: Eratosthenes
eratosthenes.epigram: He measured the world with a well and a stick.

quYuan.name: Qu Yuan
quYuan.epigram: The road is long; I will search high and low.
quYuan.kernel: The poet of the Chu Ci.

simaQian.name: Sima Qian
simaQian.epigram: He finished the Records rather than die.

phidias.name: Phidias
phidias.epigram: He put his own face on the shield.

liBing.name: Li Bing
liBing.epigram: He cut the mountain and the river obeyed.

heroOfAlexandria.name: Amanitore
heroOfAlexandria.epigram: What the raiders broke, she built again, and larger.
heroOfAlexandria.kernel: A ruling queen of Kush. With her co-ruler Natakamani she built the temples of Naqa, restored the temple of Amun that a Roman army had wrecked, and dug reservoirs at Meroë.

eupalinos.name: Pushyagupta
eupalinos.epigram: He stopped the streams under the mountain.
eupalinos.kernel: A governor under Chandragupta Maurya. He dammed the streams below Mount Girnar to make Lake Sudarshana, which watered the fields for centuries. One rock inscription names him, and that is all we have.

zhangQian.name: Zhang Qian
zhangQian.epigram: He went west and came back with the world.

nanaivandak.name: Nanaivandak
nanaivandak.kernel: The Sogdian Ancient Letters, found sealed at Dunhuang.

hippalus.name: Zoskales
hippalus.epigram: Careful with his coin, and well read.
hippalus.kernel: The ruler of the Red Sea coast around the port of Adulis, where ivory and tortoise shell were sold to ships from Egypt. A Greek sailing guide calls him tight with money, honest and well read. That one passage is all we have.

crassus.name: Crassus
crassus.epigram: No man is rich who cannot pay an army.

pytheas.name: Jang Bogo
pytheas.epigram: No ship was taken while he kept the sea.
pytheas.kernel: A Korean who served as an officer in China, then came home to Silla and built a sea fortress on the island of Wando. He drove the slave raiders from the Yellow Sea and controlled the trade between Korea, China and Japan.

hannibal.name: Hannibal
hannibal.epigram: We will find a way, or make one.

hanXin.name: Han Xin
hanXin.epigram: Backs to the river, they could not lose.

gaiusMarius.name: Gaius Marius
gaiusMarius.epigram: The road is the army, and the army carries the road.
gaiusMarius.kernel: Consul seven times; the legions that shouldered their own kit.

boudica.name: Boudica
boudica.epigram: They burned three cities before the road.

spartacus.name: Spartacus
spartacus.epigram: He left the school with kitchen knives.

ibnSina.name: Ibn Sīnā
ibnSina.epigram: Medicine is not hard; the hard part is the patient.

alKhwarizmi.name: al-Khwārizmī
alKhwarizmi.epigram: The reckoning by restoration and balancing.

maimonides.name: Maimonides
maimonides.epigram: Teach the perplexed, and the perplexity is already half gone.
maimonides.kernel: Physician to a sultan's court, and the Guide for the Perplexed.

rogerBacon.name: Roger Bacon
rogerBacon.epigram: Try it first, and argue about it after.
rogerBacon.kernel: Franciscan friar of Oxford; optics, the calendar, and a plea for experiment.

shenKuo.name: Shen Kuo
shenKuo.epigram: The needle points south, and a little east.

aryabhata.name: Āryabhaṭa
aryabhata.epigram: The earth turns; the stars do not.

murasakiShikibu.name: Murasaki Shikibu
murasakiShikibu.epigram: The world is a floating bridge of dreams.

snorriSturluson.name: Snorri Sturluson
snorriSturluson.epigram: He told the kings' lives and lost his own.

seiShonagon.name: Sei Shōnagon
seiShonagon.epigram: Things that make the heart beat faster.

alJazari.name: al-Jazarī
alJazari.epigram: It poured the wine and bowed.

suSong.name: Su Song
suSong.epigram: The tower kept the hours and the heavens.

villardDeHonnecourt.name: Villard de Honnecourt
villardDeHonnecourt.epigram: Drawn from life, and from thought.

ibnBattuta.name: Ibn Jubayr
ibnBattuta.epigram: The Rihla begins on the road.
ibnBattuta.kernel: A traveller from Valencia who wrote an account of his pilgrimage to Mecca.

marcoPolo.name: Marco Polo
marcoPolo.epigram: I have not told the half.

francescoDatini.name: Francesco Datini
francescoDatini.epigram: In the name of God and of profit.

subutai.name: Subutai
subutai.epigram: He conquered thirty nations from the saddle.

mimarSinan.name: Mimar Sinan
mimarSinan.epigram: An apprentice's mosque, a journeyman's, a master's.

tychoBrahe.name: Tycho Brahe
tychoBrahe.epigram: A brass nose, and an island for the stars.

johnDee.name: John Dee
johnDee.epigram: The angels speak in a language of their own.

copernicus.name: Copernicus
copernicus.epigram: He stopped the sun and moved the earth.

christineDePizan.name: Christine de Pizan
christineDePizan.epigram: A city of ladies, built of reason.
christineDePizan.kernel: The first professional woman of letters.

durer.name: Dürer
durer.epigram: A rhinoceros he never saw, drawn perfectly.

basho.name: Bashō
basho.epigram: Even in Kyoto, I long for Kyoto.

sorJuana.name: Sor Juana
sorJuana.epigram: I do not study to know more, but to ignore less.

leonardo.name: Leonardo
leonardo.epigram: Art is never finished, only abandoned.

taqiAlDin.name: Taqī al-Dīn
taqiAlDin.epigram: He measured the comet and they tore the tower down.

vaucanson.name: Vaucanson
vaucanson.epigram: It ate, it digested, it— well.

jakobFugger.name: Jakob Fugger
jakobFugger.epigram: Rich by the grace of God.

zhengHe.name: Zheng He
zhengHe.epigram: Seven voyages, and then the ships were burned.

willemBeukelszoon.name: Willem Beukelszoon
willemBeukelszoon.epigram: One clean cut, and the sea keeps until spring.
willemBeukelszoon.kernel: The Zeeland fisherman said to have taught the herring its barrel.

graciaMendesNasi.name: Gracia Mendes Nasi
graciaMendesNasi.epigram: She moved a whole people by ledger.

cosimoDeMedici.name: Jacques Cœur
cosimoDeMedici.epigram: To a willing heart, nothing is impossible.
cosimoDeMedici.kernel: A merchant from Bourges who traded across the Mediterranean and managed the finances of Charles VII of France.

nzingaOfNdongo.name: Nzinga of Ndongo
nzingaOfNdongo.epigram: She sat on her servant's back rather than the floor.

lautaro.name: Lautaro
lautaro.epigram: He learned their horses and turned them.

thales.name: Thales of Miletus
thales.epigram: He looked at the stars and fell in the well.
thales.kernel: The first Greek to explain nature without gods. He is said to have foretold an eclipse, and to have grown rich by renting every olive press before a good harvest.

tapputi.name: Tapputi
tapputi.epigram: Flowers, oil and water, and then again.
tapputi.kernel: A perfume maker and overseer in a royal palace, and the first chemist whose name we have.

panini.name: Pāṇini
panini.epigram: Four thousand rules, and not one word wasted.
panini.kernel: He wrote the grammar of Sanskrit in about 4,000 short rules. Linguists still study it.

luBan.name: Lu Ban
luBan.epigram: Do not show your axe at Lu Ban’s door.
luBan.kernel: A master carpenter. Chinese tradition gives him the saw, the plane and the siege ladder, and builders honour him as the patron of their trade.

theodorusOfSamos.name: Anacharsis
theodorusOfSamos.epigram: First the bellows, then the fire.
theodorusOfSamos.kernel: A Scythian prince who travelled to Athens and was counted among its wise men. The Greeks credited him with the bellows, the anchor with two flukes and the potter’s wheel. The inventions may be legend.

hanno.name: Hanno the Navigator
hanno.epigram: Past the Pillars the coast keeps going.
hanno.kernel: He took sixty ships out past the Pillars of Hercules and down the coast of West Africa to found trading towns. His report survives in Greek.

fanLi.name: Fan Li
fanLi.epigram: When the birds are gone, the bow is put away.
fanLi.kernel: A minister who helped his king win a war, then left court and made three fortunes in trade. China remembers him as the model merchant.

harkhuf.name: Harkhuf
harkhuf.kernel: A governor who led four donkey caravans south into Nubia and came back with incense, ebony and ivory. He had the story cut on his tomb.

fuHao.name: Fu Hao
fuHao.epigram: The bones asked: should Fu Hao lead? The bones said yes.
fuHao.kernel: A queen who led armies of thousands and made the royal sacrifices. The oracle bones name her, and her tomb was found whole in 1976.

sunTzu.name: Sun Tzu
sunTzu.kernel: The general to whom The Art of War is credited. Historians are not sure that he lived; the book is real and still read.

virgil.name: Virgil
virgil.epigram: So great a labour it was to found the Roman people.
virgil.kernel: The poet of the Aeneid, the story of how a band of exiles founded Rome, and of the Georgics, a poem about farming.

kalidasa.name: Kālidāsa
kalidasa.epigram: Go, cloud, and tell her I am alive.
kalidasa.kernel: The great poet and playwright of Sanskrit. In The Cloud Messenger an exile asks a cloud to carry word to his wife across all of India.

wangXizhi.name: Wang Xizhi
wangXizhi.epigram: Later men will look at us as we look at the past.
wangXizhi.kernel: The Sage of Calligraphy. His Preface to the Orchid Pavilion is the most copied piece of writing in China; the original is lost.

caiYan.name: Cai Yan
caiYan.epigram: Twelve years, and I knew every scroll.
caiYan.kernel: A poet and musician taken north by Xiongnu raiders for twelve years, then ransomed home. She wrote out her father’s lost library from memory. Which poems are hers is disputed.

juliusCaesar.name: Julius Caesar
juliusCaesar.kernel: He conquered Gaul, wrote the book about it, crossed the Rubicon and ruled Rome until the senators killed him.

zhugeLiang.name: Zhuge Liang
zhugeLiang.epigram: I gave everything, until the end.
zhugeLiang.kernel: Chancellor and strategist of the Three Kingdoms. He fed his armies from soldier farms, and tradition gives him the repeating crossbow.

trungTrac.name: Trưng Trắc
trungTrac.epigram: Sixty-five towns rose in one season.
trungTrac.kernel: With her sister Trưng Nhị she raised the country against Han rule and held sixty-five towns for three years. Vietnam honours the sisters as national heroes.

luBuwei.name: Lü Buwei
luBuwei.kernel: A merchant who backed a hostage prince as “goods worth hoarding”, put him on the throne of Qin and became chancellor.

caiLun.name: Cai Lun
caiLun.epigram: Bark, rags and old fishing nets.
caiLun.kernel: A court official who showed the emperor paper made from bark, rags and old nets in 105. The world wrote on it afterwards.

mariaHebraea.name: Maria Hebraea
mariaHebraea.epigram: One becomes two, two becomes three.
mariaHebraea.kernel: The first alchemist whose apparatus we know: the still and the water bath that cooks still call a bain-marie. Later writers quote her; no work of hers survives.

liBai.name: Li Bai
liBai.epigram: I raise my cup and ask the moon to drink.
liBai.kernel: The most loved poet of China: wine, the moon, rivers and friends who leave. Legend says he drowned reaching for the moon in the water.

dante.name: Dante Alighieri
dante.epigram: In the middle of the road of our life.
dante.kernel: An exile who wrote the Divine Comedy: a walk through Hell, Purgatory and Heaven, in the language people spoke.

ferdowsi.name: Ferdowsi
ferdowsi.epigram: I have sown the seeds of the word.
ferdowsi.kernel: He gave thirty years to the Shahnameh, the Book of Kings: every hero of Persia in fifty thousand couplets.

michelangelo.name: Michelangelo
michelangelo.epigram: The figure was in the stone already.
michelangelo.kernel: The sculptor of David, the painter of the Sistine ceiling and the architect of the dome of St Peter’s. He chose his own marble at the quarry.

ibnAlHaytham.name: Ibn al-Haytham
ibnAlHaytham.epigram: Doubt the old books. Then test.
ibnAlHaytham.kernel: He proved by experiment that we see because light enters the eye, and wrote the Book of Optics. Europe called him Alhazen.

ibnKhaldun.name: Ibn Khaldun
ibnKhaldun.epigram: The past is like the future, as water is like water.
ibnKhaldun.kernel: A judge and historian. His Muqaddimah explains why states rise, grow soft and fall, and many call it the first work of social science.

brahmagupta.name: Brahmagupta
brahmagupta.epigram: A debt taken from nothing is a fortune.
brahmagupta.kernel: The first to write rules for zero as a number, and for debts and fortunes: negative and positive numbers.

belisarius.name: Belisarius
belisarius.epigram: Give me the few, and the city.
belisarius.kernel: Justinian’s general. With small armies he took back North Africa and Italy, and he fed his wars from the towns he won.

gajahMada.name: Gajah Mada
gajahMada.epigram: No spice until the islands are one.
gajahMada.kernel: Prime minister of Majapahit. He swore to taste no spice until the whole archipelago was one, and nearly kept the oath.

amina.name: Amina of Zazzau
amina.epigram: Where she camped, a wall stood.
amina.kernel: A warrior queen who walled every camp she made and opened the trade roads north. Hausa towns still call old walls “Amina’s walls”. The sources are later chronicles and oral tradition.

tlacaelel.name: Tlacaelel
tlacaelel.epigram: Three kings ruled. One man stayed.
tlacaelel.kernel: Chief counsellor to three Mexica rulers. He shaped the Triple Alliance and the wars fought to take captives. The sources are from after the conquest.

gutenberg.name: Johannes Gutenberg
gutenberg.epigram: One letter, cast a thousand times.
gutenberg.kernel: He cast metal type, built the press and printed the Bible. He lost the workshop to his lender before the books sold.

jangYeongSil.name: Jang Yeong-sil
jangYeongSil.epigram: The rain was measured, and the harvest known.
jangYeongSil.kernel: Born a slave, raised to court by King Sejong for his skill. He built the rain gauge, a water clock that struck its own hours and star globes.

ibnMajid.name: Aḥmad ibn Mājid
ibnMajid.epigram: The sea has roads for those who can read.
ibnMajid.kernel: The master pilot of the Indian Ocean, called the Lion of the Sea. His book of winds, stars and coasts guided ships for centuries.

fatimaAlFihri.name: Fatima al-Fihri
fatimaAlFihri.epigram: She spent it all on one door that stays open.
fatimaAlFihri.kernel: A merchant’s daughter who spent her inheritance to found the mosque and school of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, which still teaches. The story comes from later writers.

hippocrates.name: Hippocrates
hippocrates.epigram: Life is short, the art long.
hippocrates.kernel: The physician who taught that illness has natural causes. Doctors still swear an oath in his name.

anaximander.name: Varāhamihira
anaximander.epigram: A foreigner who knows the stars is to be honoured.
anaximander.kernel: An astronomer of Ujjain. He set five older systems of astronomy side by side, two of them from the Greek and Roman world, and wrote that foreign scholars deserve honour for their science.

baudhayana.name: Baudhāyana
baudhayana.epigram: Stretch the cord across the square.
baudhayana.kernel: He wrote the rules for building fire altars with rope and pegs. They hold the right-angle rule, long before Greece.

peseshet.name: Peseshet
peseshet.epigram: Overseer of the women who heal.
peseshet.kernel: Her tomb stone calls her “overseer of the women physicians”: the first woman doctor whose name we have. Nothing else about her is known.

solon.name: Solon
solon.kernel: The lawgiver of Athens. He cancelled the debts that made farmers slaves, wrote the laws, and left the city for ten years so that nobody could ask him to change them.

hesiod.name: Yamanoue no Okura
hesiod.epigram: What are silver and gold beside a child?
hesiod.kernel: A court official and provincial governor in Japan. His poems speak of what other court poets left out: hungry farmers, the tax collector at the door, old age and love for his children.

aesop.name: Aesop
aesop.kernel: The teller of the fables: the fox and the grapes, the tortoise and the hare. Tradition makes him a slave who talked his way free; he may be a legend.

exekias.name: Aj Maxam
exekias.epigram: This is the painting of Aj Maxam.
exekias.kernel: A Maya vase painter of the royal house of Naranjo. He signed his cups and named his parents on them. Painted cups like his were given as gifts from one court to another.

telesilla.name: Macuilxochitzin
telesilla.epigram: The women spoke, and the wounded man lived.
telesilla.kernel: A Mexica poet, daughter of the counsellor Tlacaelel. Her one surviving song tells of a war in which an enemy warrior wounded the ruler, and of the women who pleaded for that warrior’s life. The song was written down after the conquest, and some doubt that it is hers.

thutmoseTheSculptor.name: Thutmose the Sculptor
thutmoseTheSculptor.epigram: The king’s favourite, the master of works.
thutmoseTheSculptor.kernel: The court sculptor in whose workshop the painted head of Nefertiti was found.

mandrocles.name: Artachaees
mandrocles.epigram: He cut the land so that the ships could cross it.
mandrocles.kernel: A Persian noble, said to be the tallest man in Persia. He directed the digging of a canal through the neck of Mount Athos so that the fleet of Xerxes could pass. The town where he died honoured him as a hero.

ineni.name: Ineni
ineni.epigram: No one seeing, no one hearing.
ineni.kernel: Architect to four kings. He cut the first royal tomb in the Valley of the Kings, “no one seeing, no one hearing”.

sunshuAo.name: Sunshu Ao
sunshuAo.epigram: He held the river until the fields asked for it.
sunshuAo.kernel: A minister who dammed a valley to make the Peony Dam reservoir. It still waters the fields of Anhui.

colaeus.name: Sulayman al-Tajir
colaeus.epigram: In that country they drink a leaf in hot water.
colaeus.kernel: A merchant of the Gulf port of Siraf who sailed to India and China. The first Arabic account of China, of its tea and its fine clay cups, names him as its witness. Nothing else about him is known.

wenamun.name: Wenamun
wenamun.epigram: I sat on the shore for twenty-nine days.
wenamun.kernel: A temple agent sent to buy cedar. He was robbed, ignored and made to wait, and wrote it all down. The report may be a story.

iddinMarduk.name: Iddin-Marduk
iddinMarduk.kernel: A trader of onions and barley whose tablets survive in hundreds. He bought the crop in the villages and sold it in the city.

leonidas.name: Leonidas
leonidas.kernel: The king who held the pass at Thermopylae with three hundred Spartans until all were dead.

djehuty.name: Djehuty
djehuty.epigram: Two hundred baskets, and a man in each.
djehuty.kernel: A general of Thutmose III. The tale says he took the city of Joppa with soldiers hidden in baskets.

artemisia.name: Piye
artemisia.epigram: He took the city from the water.
artemisia.kernel: A king of Kush who sailed down the Nile and conquered Egypt. His fleet took the enemy’s ships on the river, and he stormed Memphis from its harbour side. The great stone that tells the campaign also records his anger at a king who starved his horses.

tomyris.name: Tomyris
tomyris.epigram: I will give you your fill of blood.
tomyris.kernel: The queen who, in Herodotus, defeated and killed Cyrus the Great. Cyrus is a leader in this game; she is his match, not his clash.

euclid.name: Euclid
euclid.kernel: He wrote the Elements. Schools taught geometry from it for two thousand years.

banZhao.name: Ban Zhao
banZhao.epigram: The brother began it. The sister finished it.
banZhao.kernel: She finished the Book of Han after her brother died, and taught the empress and the court library’s scholars.

sophocles.name: Sophocles
sophocles.epigram: Call no man happy until he is dead.
sophocles.kernel: The playwright of Oedipus and Antigone. He won the festival of Dionysus more often than anyone.

tiruvalluvar.name: Tiruvalluvar
tiruvalluvar.epigram: Learn well, then live as you have learned.
tiruvalluvar.kernel: The poet of the Kural: 1,330 couplets on virtue, wealth and love. Tradition says he was a weaver. Little about his life is certain.

auvaiyar.name: Auvaiyar
auvaiyar.epigram: What we know is a handful of earth.
auvaiyar.kernel: A poet who walked from court to court. One of her poems is said to have stopped a war between two kings.

heronOfAlexandria.name: Hero of Alexandria
heronOfAlexandria.epigram: Light the fire, and the doors open.
heronOfAlexandria.kernel: He built a steam ball that spun, temple doors that opened by fire, and a machine that sold holy water for a coin.

apollodorus.name: Gyōki
apollodorus.epigram: Where the road stopped at a river, he built.
apollodorus.kernel: A Buddhist monk who walked the provinces of Japan with a following of ordinary people. They built bridges, roads, ponds and boat landings. The court first banned his preaching, then asked him to raise the funds for the Great Buddha of Nara.

sostratus.name: al-Hasan ibn Sulayman
sostratus.epigram: They called him the father of gifts.
sostratus.kernel: Sultan of Kilwa, the island port that held the gold trade of the Swahili coast. He built the palace of Husuni Kubwa on the cliff above the harbour and enlarged the Great Mosque. A traveller who met him wrote of his generosity.

zhengGuo.name: Zheng Guo
zhengGuo.epigram: I came to ruin you, and I have made you rich.
zhengGuo.kernel: Sent as a spy to waste Qin’s strength on a great canal. He was found out, and told the king the canal would feed Qin for ever. It did.

pasion.name: Anāthapiṇḍika
pasion.epigram: He paid for the grove by covering it in coin.
pasion.kernel: A banker of Shravasti in the time of the Buddha. The story says he bought a park for the monks at the price its owner named: enough gold coin to cover the ground. The story is from Buddhist scripture.

widowQing.name: Widow Qing of Ba
widowQing.epigram: The red stone, and the quicksilver in it.
widowQing.kernel: She ran her family’s cinnabar mines for decades. The First Emperor honoured her and built a terrace in her name. Sima Qian gives her a few lines, and that is all we have.

yarhai.name: Marcus Ulpius Yarhai
yarhai.kernel: A patron of the desert caravans between Rome and the Gulf. Palmyra raised at least ten statues to thank him. A deep cut.

sangHongyang.name: Sang Hongyang
sangHongyang.epigram: Wealth does not fall from heaven.
sangHongyang.kernel: A merchant’s son who could reckon in his head at thirteen. He set up the state trade in salt and iron and defended it in a famous debate.

moduChanyu.name: Modu Chanyu
moduChanyu.kernel: He trained his riders to shoot where his whistling arrow went, and joined the steppe into one power. He is a leader today and leaves the leaders in the chosen roster.

chanakya.name: Chanakya
chanakya.epigram: The arrow may miss. The plan does not.
chanakya.kernel: The minister who put Chandragupta on the throne. Tradition names him the author of the Arthashastra, a manual of rule, spies and war.

liQingzhao.name: Li Qingzhao
liQingzhao.kernel: The great poet of the song lyric. She and her husband collected old bronzes and rubbings, and she lost nearly all of it in flight from the war.

hildegardOfBingen.name: Hildegard of Bingen
hildegardOfBingen.epigram: A feather on the breath of God.
hildegardOfBingen.kernel: An abbess who wrote music, a play, books of medicine and letters to emperors. She is a leader today and leaves the leaders in the chosen roster. The Catholic Church honours her as a saint and teacher.

brunelleschi.name: Filippo Brunelleschi
brunelleschi.epigram: He showed them how to stand an egg on its end.
brunelleschi.kernel: He raised the dome of Florence cathedral with no wooden frame under it, with hoists of his own design.

guoShoujing.name: Guo Shoujing
guoShoujing.epigram: Water to the capital, and the year to the second.
guoShoujing.kernel: He finished the Grand Canal into Beijing, built the instruments of the observatory and measured the year to within half a minute.
